## Deviations

- The refresh lands as a NEW committed asset
  (`state_alpr_statute_seed_2026.toml`, `supersedes_asset` naming the
  2022 asset) rather than in-place rows on the old file — the ticket's
  own interface clause says the seed stays append-only in shape (a
  changed statute is a new row, never an in-place rewrite), and I8 §4.4
  prescribes a v2 asset + `seeds.toml` row. Both assets stay registered
  and loadable; the 2022 seed keeps its provenance as the `recorded`
  states' `statute_ref`.
- The AC's "every row has a non-empty origin URL" binds the
  `[[statutes]]` entries — all 8 carry one. `[[duty_rows]]` is a
  coverage table, not origin assertions: `none_recorded` rows carry no
  instrument by definition (asserting one would fabricate), and
  `recorded` rows cite the superseded committed asset as `statute_ref`
  rather than a legislature URL they were never verified at. The
  parser enforces this honestly: `none_recorded` carrying an
  instrument/origin is `ContentDrift`.
- Missouri EO 26-18's order text host returned 403 in the packet
  (I9a-F046 — recorded, not bypassed); the governor's-office listing
  dates and titles the order, so the entry cites the listing with
  `date_basis = "issued"` and the failure recorded in notes. New
  Mexico's `effective_date` is a journalism-lead date — `date_basis =
  "reported"` says so honestly (KY/CT signing dates are `signed`).
- `date_basis` is an additive v2 field beyond I8 §4.4's named list —
  the design prescribes `effective_date` but the packets recorded
  different date kinds; the field says what the date actually is
  rather than mislabel a signing/issue/report date as an effective
  date.
- No new ADR — the row executes the ticket contract + I8 §4.4's
  prescribed shape; the choices above are recorded here as deviation
  notes, not contract changes.
